newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe discussing election dates, reform.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe discussing election dates, reform.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday he was discussing with political parties the dates for elections due in 1998, including to the National Assembly, and possible reforms in the regional poll system.
He said he had already consulted leaders of his centre-right coalition and would meet leaders of the Socialist and Communist opposition in the next few days.
"On this basis, the government will make the proposals it deems necesaary," he told reporters.
Elections to the National Assembly are due in March 1998. The last poll in 1993 produced a centre-right landslide.
Regional elections are also due next year.

Juppe aides said last year the prime minister had dropped plans to make it easier to find stable majorities in the 22 regional assemblies by reforming the strict proportional representation voting system.

Proportional representation gave anti-immigration crusader Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right National Front the balance of power in some parts of the country in the last regional elections in 1992, forcing centre-right or left-wing coalitions to run minority executives with problems adopting a budget.
Maintaining the system could be seen as a favour to the Front, which has been kept out of the National Assembly by the twin-ballot first-past-the-post system used in national polls.
Juppe's Gaullist party last year rejected his suggestion to add a "dose" of proportional representation to the majority voting system for parliamentary elections.
Such a reform likely would open the National Assembly to the National Front. Le Pen won 15 percent of the vote in the 1995 presidential election.
